newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- prices end flat to lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- prices end flat to lower.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices ended Friday's lackluster session unchanged to slightly weaker as players looked toward next week's $3.5 billion of scheduled new issues.
"There were some reasonable bids on some bid wanteds, but it (was) just sort of a lackadaisical day," one trader said. "Net, net maybe its down 1/8, 1/4, but it's extremely quiet."
A municipal analyst said the market closed flat to down 1/8 point. High-grade issues ended unchanged, while dollar bonds closed down 1/8 point.

Friday's actively quoted issues included Jefferson County, Ala., 5-3/8 percent sewer revenue refunding bonds of February 2027. The bonds had a 5.66 percent net bid, a basis point weaker than Thursday's closing net bid of 5.65 percent.
Denver, Colo., City and County Airport 5-1/2 percent revenue bonds of November 2025 had a 5.73 percent net bid, two basis points firmer than Thursday's closing net bid of 5.75 percent.

In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond closed up 6/32 at 99-26/32 to yield 6.64 percent. In debt futures, the March municipal contract closed down 2/32 at 117-5/32. The March T-bond contract closed down 3/32 at 112-30/32. The MOB spread was 135 ticks.
On the economic front, Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan is scheduled to deliver the first leg of his semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins testimony to Congress on Wednesday.

"I guess you always have the possibility of him saying something and being misconstrued," the trader said, adding however that the limited inflation, reasonable growth theme is likely to prevail. "I don't think he's going to be saying too much to scare the market too much."

Turning to new issues, $3.5 billion of fresh debt is expected to arrive in 108 deals next week. Sixty-five competitive deals are expected, totaling $1.13 billion. Forty-three negotiated sales are slated, totaling $2.38 billion.

"I think it will be nice to have some supply and, you know, I think there is still some money out there," a trader said. "The deals should do okay, I mean it depends on what the dollar does (and) governments hanging in there."
Five of those negotiated offerings are expected to total $150 million or more. Morgan Stanley & Co is expected to price $490 million New York City Municipal Assistance Corp bonds.
Goldman Sachs is expected to price $260 million New York State Thruway Authority bonds, while Smith Barney Inc is set to bring a $250 million Cook County, Ill., deal.
Also next week, Smith Barney is expected to price $250 million San Diego Public Facilities Financial Authority, Calif, bonds and $150 million Platte River Power Authority, Colo., bonds.
On the competitive side, a $240 million Maryland offering tops the list.
